newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end bourse ahead, dollar supports.
newsitem.headline: German equities end bourse ahead, dollar supports.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade in Frankfurt on Monday slightly higher, lifted early on by Friday's strong close on Wall St, but a tendancy towards consolidation held the market off further meaningful gains.
The DAX index, which measures trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, ended floor trade up 7.85 points, or 0.29 percent, at 2,693.88.

Early last week the DAX index reached record highs above the psychological and technical level of 2,700, but then fell back somewhat. The dollar held just above the crucial 1.53 mark level, boosting export-oriented German stocks.

During the session on Monday the chemicals sector was a favourite, dealers said, with Bayer AG ending up 36 pfennigs at 58.21, BASF AG up 58 pfennigs at 49.66 and Hoechst AG gaining 57 pfennigs to stand at 58.32.
Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, in the spotlight since last week on talk that Deutsche Bank AG has upped its ownership in the Bavarian bank, ended up 47 pfennigs at 55.69.

Amongst the medium-sized firms engineering company Deutsche Babcock AG ended nearly nine percent lower, falling 4.50 marks to 47.40 after it said it would incur a higher charge for its restructuring measures than originally expected.
New stock Fresenius Medical Care AG continued to attract interest on the MDAX index of medium-sized companies, rising 5.80 marks to 122.60.
Pharmaceuticals firm Gehe AG climbed 2.60 marks to 107.60 after it said it would sell off a generic drugs unit.

Meanwhile lead creditor Deutsche Bank of Traub AG sought the suspension of the engineering company's stock. The firm said it faced serious liqidity problems and its creditors would meet later on Monday.
